chunks: From him, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Ribāṭ, from Ibn Miskān, who said:
The one who asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام narrated to me about a man upon whom prayers had accumulated. He said: “Cast them off and begin anew.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: There is no contradiction between the two reports, because it is possible that the first report is specific to the obligatory prayers, in which case one must investigate and make them up, while the second report is specific to the supererogatory prayers, in which case it is permissible for him to leave them. And if we were to interpret both of them as referring to the supererogatory prayers, then it would be possible to understand the first report as recommendation and the second as permissibility.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: salat (prayer), here referring to prayers that have accumulated upon a person
key_terms.وَيَقْضِيَ: to make up missed acts of worship
key_terms.يَتَحَرَّى: to investigate carefully and determine as best as possible

ai.seo_question: How do Shia hadith reconcile differing reports about accumulated prayers and making them up?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling on accumulated prayers and how apparently differing narrations may be reconciled. Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan explains that one report may concern obligatory prayers, which must be sought out and made up, while the other may concern supererogatory prayers, which may be left; alternatively, both may refer to supererogatory prayers, with one indicating recommendation and the other permissibility.
